To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) label noise causes a double descent peak for ridgeless linear regression in the overparameterized regime, (b) this peak is universal for a broad class of feature maps, and (c) the peak can be avoided by regularizing the loss.

In the presence of label (classification) noise, the interpolation threshold of ridgeless linear regression (i.e., the point where the generalization error starts to increase) is strictly above the interpolation threshold of ordinary least squares regression (OLS).

(1) ridgeless linear regression performs poorly around the interpolation threshold, (2) this is a universal phenomenon that applies to a large class of input distributions and feature maps and (3) our theory is able to explain the poor performance of ridgeless linear regression around the interpolation threshold in a broad variety of settings, including random deep neural networks
